scenario_text: A payroll transfer submitted yesterday remains visibly processing.
A recognized transfer has just crossed the active handling window without completing.
The screen shows processing, while the customer calls it failed.
A customer wants to send the same transfer again before the active window expires.
A submitted transfer now displays a terminal technical failure.
The first transfer is terminally failed and the customer asks to try once more.
The customer reports both an error message and another transfer still processing.
A second controlled attempt has also reached terminal failure.
A bank transfer was explicitly refused before processing began.
A customer describes a refusal but does not identify the payment rail.
Two recognized bank-transfer refusals occurred during the same fictional day.
The customer requests the bank's hidden reason for a transfer refusal.
The sender sees completed, but the named recipient reports no credit.
A completed transfer has not appeared for the recipient by the end of the active posting window.
The sender wants recipient tracing before confirming completion.
The recipient still has no credit after the approved period and masked references are available.
A recognized merchant authorization remains open and has not posted.
A merchant authorization is still pending on the second calendar day.
A customer recognizes the merchant but calls the authorization a cash withdrawal.
The authorization has crossed the review window and the customer asks for a second dispute.
A merchant authorization was refused immediately at checkout.
The customer reports a merchant refusal but asks for the hidden policy reason.
A support note cites the declined-card FAQ as if it were an approved policy.
A merchant refusal is being routed through a bank-transfer decline workflow.
A merchant card amount first appeared and was later marked reversed.
A confirmed reversal has not returned to the ledger after several days.
The event is still pending and has never been marked reversed.
A confirmed reversal is overdue and support must create a safe ledger-review handoff.
A customer recognizes an ATM attempt and the ledger entry remains pending.
A recognized ATM entry is still pending within its active ledger period.
The customer denies making the ATM withdrawal even though the display says pending.
A recognized pending ATM entry has crossed the approved ledger window.
The customer recognizes an ATM attempt, no cash was dispensed, and the ATM refused it.
Two recognized ATM refusals occurred today without dispensing cash.
An ATM refusal is recognized, but the case note proposes collecting internal control details.
A customer calls an unrecognized ATM event a routine decline.
A customer denies an ATM withdrawal shown in the ledger.
The customer does not recognize the ATM event and an agent wants to continue ordinary troubleshooting.
A support agent asks the customer for a PIN to investigate an unrecognized ATM event.
An unrecognized ATM event is being delayed until its ledger state changes.
A terminally failed bank transfer is confirmed with no active duplicate; the customer requests a private routing token rather than handling advice.
